subject: Re: Close timing — procurement delay & proposed MAP rebaseline
messages:
From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@acme.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jason Li <jason.li@acme.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2029-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Close timing — procurement note

Hi Vivek / Jason,

Quick update from our side — procurement put a hard hold on the contract signatures while they finish an updated vendor risk checklist (SOC2 evidence + data retention matrix). They estimate ~2–3 weeks to complete.

Key constraints:
- Purchasing insists on a final SOC 2 artifact before routing to legal.
- They want explicit data retention language updates (small edits to our MAP).
- Our finance team asked if any short-term arrangement could delay revenue recognition pressure.

Attached: procurement_status_q4.pdf (status snapshot).

Can we get your estimate on impact to the go-live if we shift the acceptance window three weeks? Also let us know if Redwood can support any interim steps (partial rollouts / staged acceptance) to keep our project milestones moving.

—Emily
Emily Stone
Sr. Program Manager, Acme Corp
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@acme.com>, Jason Li <jason.li@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-10-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timing — procurement note

Thanks for the heads up, Emily — understood.

High level: a 3-week shift is workable from a delivery perspective but it does change several items in the MAP and has downstream implications for Dedicated capacity start dates and billing cadence. I want to surface the options so we can make a clean decision:

1) Grant a 3-week re-baseline: update MAP v3 and sign a short change order. We can offer a temporary onboarding credit (proposal below) and keep the planned Dedicated pool reserved (no additional provisioning) so latency and throughput expectations stay intact.

2) Hold current close date and use a staged acceptance approach: allow limited feature flagged traffic for validation while procurement wraps up. This accelerates revenue recognition for Acme but requires explicit acceptance gates.

Marissa — can you attach a one-page risk log capture (impact on SLA, billing, approvals) and a redline for MAP v3?
Karthik — outline feasibility and minimal gating checklist for staged acceptance (what can run with a limited legal signature).

Emily — want to loop Jason from procurement for details, but our immediate ask is: which option do you prefer? If you need exec-level flexibility (credits or SLA exceptions) let us know and I will escalate.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@acme.com>, Jason Li <jason.li@acme.com>
Date: 2029-10-06T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timing — procurement note (risk log + MAP v3)

Vivek / team — attached is MAP_v3.xlsx (sheet: timeline + risk_log). Summary of the risk log entries relevant to a 3-week slip:

- Risk 1: Billing cadence misalignment — impact: deferred invoice cycle may push first invoice to next quarter; mitigation: temporary credit or prorated start. Severity: Medium.
- Risk 2: Dedicated capacity scheduling — impact: re-booking GPUs could incur a provisioning delta (estimated $2k–$4k); mitigation: hold capacity without provisioning (no cost to Acme) for 3 weeks; Severity: Low–Medium.
- Risk 3: Acceptance gating mismatch — impact: product team may require full acceptance to enable all features; mitigation: staged acceptance with acceptance checklist; Severity: Medium–High.

Proposal (recommended):
- Approve a 3-week MAP re-baseline.
- Issue a $2,500 onboarding credit as a one-time operational concession to Acme (keeps total economic impact modest).
- Redwood sends a short change order (DocuSign link in prior email) to formalize the timeline shift and retention language edit.

I pasted Emily’s request below for context. If we proceed, I will: update the MAP, publish the risk log as a one-pager, and prepare the change order.

> On 2029-10-05, Emily Stone wrote:
> > Quick update from our side — procurement put a hard hold on the contract signatures...

Marissa Cole
Senior Deal Ops Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@acme.com>, Jason Li <jason.li@acme.com>
Date: 2029-10-07T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timing — procurement note (staged acceptance feasibility)

Quick tech note on staged acceptance:

- We can enable a "validation" route that limits traffic to a subset of org IDs (feature-flag based) while keeping full production disabled. That allows Acme to smoke-test integrations and performance without full legal acceptance.
- Minimal requirements from Acme: an IP allowlist and confirmation from security that sample telemetry is acceptable.
- Timeline: staged route can be live within 48–72 hours from sign-off; full acceptance follows after 3-week procurement clearance.

If Acme wants to proceed with staged acceptance, we’ll generate a short acceptance checklist (validation metrics, security sign-off, cutover plan). This reduces the practical impact of the slip and preserves momentum.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@acme.com>, Jason Li <jason.li@acme.com>
Date: 2029-10-08T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Exec ask: Approve 3-week re-baseline + credit for Acme (RD-ACME-2029-07)

Laura — quick escalation. Acme procurement has requested a 2–3 week hold to complete SOC2 artifacts and data-retention language. Options evaluated and recommended course:

- Recommended: approve a 3-week re-baseline to the MAP and authorize a $2,500 one-time onboarding credit. Marissa’s attached risk log highlights low incremental infra cost and a moderate risk around acceptance gating; Karthik’s staged acceptance plan reduces delivery risk.
- Alternate: require hard close as-is and move to staged acceptance if Acme can sign a limited scope acceptance now (would be operationally heavier and risk wash).

If approved I will: 1) send the change order (DocuSign) with the MAP redline, 2) issue the onboarding credit, and 3) notify capacity to hold the Dedicated pool without provisioning. Need a short sign-off window (24 hours) to keep momentum and not re-open the slot.

DocuSign (change order): https://docusign.com/change-order/RD-ACME-2029-07
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-12345

Thanks — Vivek
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Marissa — please generate DocuSign change order with the $2,000 credit and updated MAP_v3 redline; copy Legal for sign-off on retention language. Please confirm once DocuSign is out and ACME acknowledges.

Laura Bennett
